raw_plan.interpretation: I interpret this as a one-email acquisition introduction for a product manager who does not yet use Balsamiq. The email should sell one concrete workflow and drive one action: starting the documented free trial.

intent.desired_action: Start a 14-day free trial and turn one proposed flow into an interactive prototype.

raw_plan.reader: A product manager considering how to represent one proposed feature or internal-tool flow before engineering work begins.
raw_plan.reader_segment: Product manager planning a new feature or internal tool
raw_plan.reader_scope: Limit the argument to product managers who could use a prompt or screenshot to draft one proposed flow and turn it into an interactive prototype. Do not generalize this fit to every product manager or imply the recipient has a particular incumbent tool.
raw_plan.promise: Balsamiq can turn a product manager's rough idea or screenshot into an interactive version of a proposed flow without requiring code.
raw_plan.orientation: Balsamiq is a wireframing and prototyping tool a product manager can use to draft a proposed flow and share it with reviewers before engineering work starts.
raw_plan.arc: In one self-contained email, move from a concrete product operation—a prompt or screenshot becoming an interactive prototype—to a low-commitment invitation to try that operation on one real flow.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: One email leaves no room for a broad feature tour. Lead with the documented workflow most closely matched to this reader's job, answer the immediate concern about coding or committing budget, and make the 14-day no-card trial the single next step. No researched pain is used because the recipient's current workflow and difficulties are unconfirmed. The single thing that would most change this campaign: What measurable result do customers get, and how do you know?

emails.selection_reason: This is the clearest supported introduction for the selected reader: it applies Balsamiq's prompt-or-screenshot workflow directly to a product manager's proposed flow, then lets the reader test it without a purchase commitment.

value_case.reader_benefit: For a proposed feature or internal tool, the reader can give stakeholders something interactive to examine before that flow becomes engineering work.
value_case.mechanism: Balsamiq AI accepts a rough prompt or dropped-in screenshot as the starting point, and Balsamiq can turn the resulting rough wireframe into an interactive prototype without code.
decision_conditions: The trial lasts 14 days and requires no credit card.
The email should propose testing one flow; it must not imply unlimited AI capacity or unlimited projects.

claim_conditions: Frame the workflow as a supported option for a proposed flow, not proof that it suits every product manager or project.

emails.mechanism: The reader supplies a rough prompt or screenshot to Balsamiq AI, then develops the rough wireframe into an interactive prototype inside Balsamiq without writing code.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: This is a supported secondary proposition for product managers who already work with an MCP-compatible tool and want that tool to operate on the product context captured in their Balsamiq boards.

value_case.mechanism: The Balsamiq MCP server lets Claude, Cursor, and other compatible tools read, edit, and build on Balsamiq boards.
decision_conditions: This proposition is relevant only when the reader uses or is evaluating an MCP-compatible tool.
